summary.title: Port structure.dependency-cycles (ADP verdict)
summary.what: Added structure.dependency-cycles: a Corpus-altitude verdict emitting one finding per Tarjan SCC import cycle, consuming Structure.over(corpus).dependency_cycles(). Added a new BREAK_DEPENDENCY_CYCLE action to the finding ontology. Default ERROR; registered (registry 12); 5 tests.
summary.why: Recovers the legacy `deps` ADP rule onto v3. A cycle is a hard defect with a singular goal (break it) and an open mechanism — the REDUCE_COMPLEXITY shape — so it is a directed-corrective verdict that can fail the build, not a REVIEW.
summary.user_goal: Port the dependency-cycles rule (legacy deps, ADP/Martin) onto v3: Corpus-altitude verdict, one finding per import cycle, new directed action BREAK_DEPENDENCY_CYCLE at default ERROR (user-confirmed: cycles can fail CI, parallel to REDUCE_COMPLEXITY's goal-singular/mechanism-open shape). Consumes Structure.over(corpus).dependency_cycles() (Tarjan SCC, proven working). Legacy dependencies.py as oracle.

decisions.point: ERROR (can fail CI) vs REVIEW (caps WARNING) for cycles
decisions.chose: Directed BREAK_DEPENDENCY_CYCLE action at default ERROR
decisions.rationale: A cycle is an unambiguous defect with a singular goal; only the mechanism is open, exactly like REDUCE_COMPLEXITY. Preserves the legacy CI-gating of the canonical ADP violation. User-confirmed.
rejected: REVIEW verdict (would silently remove slop's ability to fail CI on cycles)
